resume.title: Profile
resume.intro: Full-Stack & Security Engineer working across enterprise platforms, industrial IoT, AI integration and offensive security research. I ship production apps (solar energy, SCADA, business comms) and run contracted + independent security research with coordinated disclosure on large SaaS platforms. Firmware/hardware reverse engineering and analysis of modern anti-tamper stacks (kernel, hypervisor, UEFI). Pursuing a Computer Science degree.

highlights: Enterprise Solar Platform (MultiluzSolarWebCalculadora): React, Node.js, Socket.IO, Google Cloud (BigQuery, Secret Manager), multi-DB (MSSQL/MySQL), digital signatures, doc generation, task scheduling.
Industrial SCADA System (MTZ_View): React 19, TypeScript, PostgreSQL. Raspberry Pi + Docker deployment. Real-time Modbus TCP/IP telemetry + alarm management.
WhatsApp Cloud API SaaS (wacraft-client): Angular 19, Rete.js (visual workflows), ApexCharts.
Bun + React 19 + Minio PWA (gpml-pwa): offline-first, Web Push notifications.
AI integration: RAG in production, local LLM hosting, model deployment for enterprise use.
Migrated performance-critical C++ components to Rust for memory safety + efficiency gains.
Worked across low- and high-level stacks (C, C++, Rust, Python) in an English-speaking remote team.
Automated build, delivery and QA processes to improve reliability.

fullstack.title: Full-Stack
fullstack.description: End-to-end architecture with multi-tenant isolation from day one, hierarchical RBAC enforced at API, query and row level via PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, and full-stack observability through OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana and Loki. Backends in Node.js and Bun with strict TypeScript, Go with Fiber or Chi for compiled APIs, C++ and Rust when latency and throughput matter. Data on PostgreSQL with pgvector for semantic search, Redis Cluster for cache and queues, ClickHouse for analytical workloads, NATS or Kafka for event streaming.
fullstack.detailed: Frontends in React 19, Vue 3, Nuxt or SvelteKit with strict typing, SSR / SSG / ISR via Vite or Turbopack, design systems built on Tailwind and shadcn/ui. Containerization with Docker + BuildKit, orchestration on Kubernetes or Nomad, infrastructure as code via Terraform and Pulumi, GitOps with Argo CD or Flux. CI/CD on GitHub Actions and GitLab Pipelines, edge delivery through Cloudflare and Fastly. OpenAPI / AsyncAPI contracts, Swagger UI, contract tests via Pact, schema-driven types end to end.

lowlevel.title: Low-Level & Reverse Engineering
lowlevel.description: Systems engineering in C23, modern C++ (C++20/23) and Rust, with first-principles understanding of memory models, concurrency primitives and ABI boundaries. Reverse engineering of x86, x86_64, ARM and ARM64 binaries; firmware and microcode analysis (AMD F32, RS64); IDA Pro processor module and loader development; dynamic instrumentation with Frida and DynamoRIO; coverage-guided fuzzing with AFL++, libFuzzer and honggfuzz; protocol reverse engineering and vulnerability isolation through differential analysis.
lowlevel.detailed: Toolchain: IDA Pro, Ghidra, Binary Ninja, radare2 / rizin, x64dbg, GDB / LLDB with pwndbg and GEF, QEMU + Unicorn for cross-arch emulation, Wireshark and tshark, Frida and DynamoRIO for hooking, BinDiff and Diaphora for binary diffing, angr and Triton for symbolic execution. Linux kernel internals (eBPF, KASAN, KCSAN), virtualization (KVM, Xen) and hypervisor-level instrumentation.

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence
ai.description: End-to-end applied-AI infrastructure: LLM fine-tuning with LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA and full-parameter SFT via Hugging Face TRL, Axolotl and Unsloth on A100 / H100 / MI300X. RAG pipelines with dense embeddings (sentence-transformers, BGE-M3, E5-Mistral, Voyage), hybrid sparse-dense retrieval (BM25 + Reciprocal Rank Fusion) and cross-encoder rerankers (bge-reranker-v2, Cohere Rerank). Vector stores on pgvector, Qdrant, Milvus and Weaviate. Inference orchestration with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp and Ollama; structured generation through Outlines, XGrammar and JSON Schema constraints.
ai.detailed: Multi-step agents with tool use and function calling (OpenAI function calling, Anthropic tool use, MCP servers), evaluation pipelines via Ragas, DeepEval and TruLens (faithfulness, context recall, answer relevance) and observability through LangSmith, Langfuse and Helicone. Production deployments mixing proprietary (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Cerebras) and open-source (Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, Mistral, DeepSeek) models with prompt caching, semantic caching, KV-cache reuse, speculative decoding and per-tenant token observability.

linux.title: Linux & Infrastructure
linux.description: Deep admin and engineering across Arch, Debian, Ubuntu, NixOS and Kali. systemd unit authoring, cgroup v2 resource isolation, namespace and seccomp-bpf sandboxing. Performance tuning with perf, eBPF (bcc, bpftrace, libbpf), flame graphs and the BPF Compiler Collection. Production incident response with structured logging through journald, Loki and Vector, and distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry. Custom kernel patches, out-of-tree modules and DRM driver work for unsupported hardware (AMD F32 microcode, BC-250 APU).

security.title: Security & Compliance
security.description: Encryption at rest and in transit: AES-256-GCM column-level on credentials and sensitive data via libsodium with envelope encryption through AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault; TLS 1.3 end-to-end with HSTS preload, OCSP stapling and modern cipher suites only. Argon2id for password hashing, secrets in environment variables or KMS-backed stores, never in the database. Mandatory MFA + RBAC with least privilege: TOTP (RFC 6238) and FIDO2 / WebAuthn (YubiKey) for owner, admin and developer roles; OAuth 2.1 + OIDC with PKCE, signed JWTs (EdDSA / ES256) and centralized policy enforcement via OPA or Casbin, with internal access reviews.
security.detailed: GDPR / LGPD / CPRA aligned: public privacy notice, data subject access / export / deletion endpoints, minimum retention per data type, deauth provider within 24h, DPIA for high-risk processing. Continuous scanning: OWASP ZAP + Nuclei (DAST), Semgrep + CodeQL (SAST), Trivy + Grype container and SBOM (CycloneDX / SPDX) scanning, gitleaks + TruffleHog secret detection, quarterly and on every material release. Dependabot + Renovate for SCA. Sigstore / cosign signed artifacts with SLSA-style supply-chain hardening. Vulnerability SLAs: critical 7 days, high 14 days, medium 30 days. Aligned with NIST SP 800-53 and CIS benchmarks.

devops.title: DevOps & Platform
devops.description: Infrastructure as code with Terraform for everything provisionable (clusters, DNS, object storage, IAM, CDN, secrets backends) versioned and reconciled through CI, no ClickOps. Orchestration on Kubernetes when the workload justifies it, k3s for smaller fleets running on Hetzner or DigitalOcean boxes. Helm for shipping internal apps as charts with per-env values, ArgoCD reconciling git → cluster so the manifest is the source of truth, not whatever was last kubectl-apply'd at 3am.
devops.detailed: Edge with Nginx or Traefik: TLS termination, gzip/brotli, request coalescing, rate limits, mTLS to upstreams; Cloudflare in front when DDoS protection matters. Stateful pieces self-hosted when control matters: Redis (primary + sentinel-failover replica, RDB + AOF), PostgreSQL (streaming replication, PITR via WAL archive, pgBouncer), Minio for S3-compatible blob storage. Observability via Prometheus + Grafana + Loki + OpenTelemetry, single trace ID from browser → nginx → pod → redis → postgres. CI/CD via GitHub Actions and GitLab CI: multi-stage Docker builds, Trivy + Grype vuln scans gating prod, cosign-signed artifacts, automatic rollback on failing readiness probes. Secrets in Vault or KMS-backed env injection, never in repo.

bc250.title: bc250 bios recolour
intro: repaints the colours the AMD BC-250 BIOS uses for
its menus and dialogs. runs entirely in your browser
the ROM is never uploaded anywhere.
bc250.drop: drop a .ROM here, or click to pick one
warning: every index is editable, but only a few change anything
you will see. 0 paints section headings, the boot screen
and the shell. 1 is the body text and the dialog behind
it. 7 is the screen. 8 is the read-only fields, 15 the
editable values. keep each pair readable against the
other and use 'show the original' before you flash.
bc250.verifyNote: the result is reopened and checked before download
risk: you are modding a BIOS at your own risk. a power cut
mid-flash or the wrong board revision leaves the machine
dead until you reflash the chip externally. do not do this
without a hardware programmer on hand.
bc250.ack: i have a CH341A (or equivalent SPI programmer) and i take responsibility for any brick

does not scale it, so the canvas is the only thing that
decides how big it lands. 1024x768 is tested; beyond that
the build refuses if it no longer fits the volume. 1x1 is
how other images ship with no splash at all.
